note: Our own programs on a stock C64, so no third-party rights arise and 198x/decisions/capturing-published-software.md does not bite. The three programs are the ones in the entry, unmodified, plus a machine-code equivalent written for the comparison.

captures.claim: Filling the screen takes BASIC seconds and machine code less than one frame — so the gap that matters is the interpreter, not the choice of BASIC statement.
captures.composite: Three captures, one per method, each taken exactly 50 frames (1.0s PAL) after the program body begins, then composited into a single labelled figure. Published with frame="none" because it is a composition rather than a single screen; the panels themselves are unretouched captures.

programs.print: 5 POKE 678,1 / 10 PRINT CHR$(147); / 20 FOR I=1 TO 1000 / 30 PRINT "A"; / 40 NEXT I
programs.poke: 5 POKE 678,1 / 10 FOR I=1024 TO 2023 / 20 POKE I,1 / 30 NEXT I
programs.machine_code: lda #$01 / ldx #$00 / loop: sta $0400,x / sta $0500,x / sta $0600,x / sta $0700,x / inx / bne loop / rts — poked to $C000 and called with SYS 49152

captures.post: crop each panel to the 320x200 active area at (48,56) of the 416x312 raster, nearest-neighbour x2, then stack with labels

measurements.tested_claim: "Time: Approximately 18 seconds (PAL C64)" for PRINT, "Approximately 2 seconds" for POKE, "Result: POKE is 9 times faster for this simple task."
measurements.verdict: All three figures were wrong, and the comparison was between the wrong pair. PRINT takes 2.5s, POKE takes 4.3s — so POKE is slower, not nine times faster — and machine code does the same job in 6.5ms.
measurements.method: Both BASIC programs typed with type_string (load_basic_program has no C64 handler) and run on a cold machine. A sentinel byte at 678 is zeroed before RUN and set by the program's first line; a second at 679 is set by its last. Frame counts are read from machine.frame_count and the sentinels polled with memory_read every 5 frames, so the timing brackets the program body and excludes typing and BASIC's own startup. Granularity is +/- 5 frames, or 0.1s.

results.machine_code: 256 iterations x (4x STA abs,X at 5 cycles + INX at 2 + BNE at 3) = 6,400 cycles, about 6.5ms at 985kHz PAL — under a third of one frame. Verified by screenshot: the fill is complete in the single frame following SYS.

measurements.why: Not measured, stated as mechanism rather than finding: POKE I,1 in a FOR loop re-evaluates a floating-point loop variable into an address on every pass, work PRINT does not do. Both are dominated by interpreter overhead rather than by the screen write itself, which is why neither is close to the machine-code figure.
measurements.provenance_of_the_correction: Raised by Steve, who said he had seen screen fills run far faster than the measurement suggested and that the approach looked flawed. He was right about the mechanism and it sharpened the finding: the fast case he remembered is the machine-code one, which the entry never measured and which is 660x the BASIC POKE loop. The first framing of this measurement — 'POKE is slower than PRINT' — was too broad, since that holds only for these two BASIC loops.

still_unmeasured: Several figures elsewhere in the entry remain unverified and are inherited, not checked: the score-display timings of ~50ms (PRINT), ~10ms (POKE) and ~3ms (optimised POKE), and the 'dozens of operations per character' / 'one operation per character' summary. Given the headline numbers were wrong by an order of magnitude and in the wrong direction, these should be measured before they are trusted. The same harness would do it.
